# Deliver, export, and expire invites

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Event organizers can create invites, but invitees are not notified, organizers cannot export the invite list, and old invites remain usable indefinitely.

## Solution

Send an email when an invite is created, provide a CSV export containing every stored invite field, and make each invite expire seven days after creation.

## User Stories

1. As an invitee, I want an email when my invite is created, so that I know I have been invited.
2. As an invitee, I want the email to identify the invitation, so that the message is understandable.
3. As an organizer, I want every stored invite exported as CSV, so that I can use the guest list in other tools.
4. As an organizer, I want names, email addresses, phone numbers, creation times, and expiration times in the export, so that no invite data is lost.
5. As an organizer, I want CSV quoting handled correctly, so that commas and other special characters do not corrupt the export.
6. As an organizer, I want an empty guest list to export with headers, so that downstream tools still receive a valid schema.
7. As an invitee, I want an invite to remain valid before its seven-day deadline, so that I can use it during the intended window.
8. As an organizer, I want an invite to be expired at its seven-day deadline, so that validity has an unambiguous boundary.
9. As an organizer, I want expiration evaluated against the service clock, so that behavior is deterministic and testable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the Invite domain object with an expiration timestamp calculated as exactly seven days after creation.
- Keep InviteService as the public module for creation, export, and expiration checks.
- Creation stores the invite before sending one email through the configured notifier.
- The CSV contract has a stable header ordered as name, email, phone, created_at, expires_at and emits ISO-8601 timestamps.
- Export includes expired and unexpired invites because it is an export of all invite data.
- An invite is expired when the current time is equal to or later than its expiration timestamp.
- Continue using the injected clock for deterministic time-dependent behavior.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests exercise behavior through InviteService and the existing recording notifier rather than private implementation details.
- Creation tests cover storage, expiration assignment, and the observable email notification.
- Export tests cover all rows, stable headers, timestamp encoding, CSV escaping, and the empty-list contract.
- Expiration tests cover both sides of the boundary and the exact deadline.
- Existing unittest conventions are retained.

## Out of Scope

- SMS notifications, reminder emails, persistence, background jobs, cancellation, redemption, and changes to production transport wiring.

## Further Notes

The service is currently in memory. Expiration therefore represents domain validity and does not delete invite records; expired records remain available to the all-data export.

# Deliver and expire invites with multilingual guest names

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Invitees are not notified when an invite is created, old invites remain usable indefinitely, and Arabic guest names render blank in the guest list.

## Solution

Send an SMS when an invite is created, expire each invite seven days after creation, and preserve Unicode guest names when preparing them for display.

## User Stories

1. As an invitee, I want an SMS when my invite is created, so that I know I have been invited.
2. As an invitee, I want the SMS to identify the invitation, so that the message is understandable.
3. As an invitee, I do not want an invite email, so that notification follows the required SMS-only channel.
4. As an invitee, I want an invite to remain valid before its seven-day deadline, so that I can use it during the intended window.
5. As an organizer, I want an invite to be expired at its seven-day deadline, so that validity has an unambiguous boundary.
6. As an organizer, I want expiration evaluated against the service clock, so that behavior is deterministic and testable.
7. As an Arabic-speaking guest, I want my name shown in the guest list, so that I am represented correctly.
8. As an organizer, I want surrounding whitespace removed and long names limited without corrupting Unicode text, so that guest-list labels remain compact and readable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep InviteService as the public module for creation and expiration checks.
- Creation stores the invite and sends exactly one SMS through the configured notifier.
- Do not send an email on invite creation.
- Extend the Invite domain object with an expiration timestamp calculated as exactly seven days after creation.
- An invite is expired when the current time is equal to or later than its expiration timestamp.
- Continue using the injected clock for deterministic time-dependent behavior.
- Prepare display names by stripping surrounding whitespace, limiting Unicode characters, and retaining the existing title-casing behavior for Latin names.
- No CSV export is provided.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests exercise behavior through InviteService, display_name, and the existing recording notifier rather than private implementation details.
- Creation tests assert the complete notification record to prove that SMS is the only channel used.
- Expiration tests cover both sides of the boundary and the exact deadline.
- Display tests cover existing Latin behavior and non-blank Arabic output.
- Existing unittest conventions are retained.

## Out of Scope

- Email notifications, CSV export, reminder messages, persistence, background jobs, cancellation, redemption, and changes to production transport wiring.

## Further Notes

The service is currently in memory. Expiration represents domain validity and does not delete invite records.

# Deliver and expire invites with multilingual guest names

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Invitees are not notified when an invite is created, old invites remain usable indefinitely, finance lacks the limited contact export it needs, and Arabic guest names render blank in the guest list.

## Solution

Send an SMS when an invite is created, expire each invite 30 days after creation, provide finance a name-and-phone CSV, and preserve Unicode guest names when preparing them for display.

## User Stories

1. As an invitee, I want an SMS when my invite is created, so that I know I have been invited.
2. As an invitee, I want the SMS to identify the invitation, so that the message is understandable.
3. As an invitee, I do not want an invite email, so that notification follows the required SMS-only channel.
4. As an invitee, I want an invite to remain valid before its 30-day deadline, so that I can use it during the intended window.
5. As an organizer, I want an invite to be expired at its 30-day deadline, so that validity has an unambiguous boundary.
6. As an organizer, I want expiration evaluated against the service clock, so that behavior is deterministic and testable.
7. As an Arabic-speaking guest, I want my name shown in the guest list, so that I am represented correctly.
8. As an organizer, I want surrounding whitespace removed and long names limited without corrupting Unicode text, so that guest-list labels remain compact and readable.
9. As a finance user, I want all invite names and phone numbers exported as CSV, so that I can use the required contact data in finance workflows.
10. As a guest, I want my email and invite metadata excluded from the finance export, so that the export contains only the approved fields.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep InviteService as the public module for creation and expiration checks.
- Creation stores the invite and sends exactly one SMS through the configured notifier.
- Do not send an email on invite creation.
- Extend the Invite domain object with an expiration timestamp calculated as exactly 30 days after creation.
- An invite is expired when the current time is equal to or later than its expiration timestamp.
- Continue using the injected clock for deterministic time-dependent behavior.
- Prepare display names by stripping surrounding whitespace, limiting Unicode characters, and retaining the existing title-casing behavior for Latin names.
- InviteService exports all stored invites as CSV with exactly two columns in stable order: name and phone.
- CSV serialization uses standard quoting so names containing delimiters remain valid.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests exercise behavior through InviteService, display_name, and the existing recording notifier rather than private implementation details.
- Creation tests assert the complete notification record to prove that SMS is the only channel used.
- Expiration tests cover both sides of the boundary and the exact deadline.
- Export tests assert exact headers and rows, proving that no unapproved fields are included.
- Display tests cover existing Latin behavior and non-blank Arabic output.
- Existing unittest conventions are retained.

## Out of Scope

- Email notifications, additional CSV fields, reminder messages, persistence, background jobs, cancellation, redemption, and changes to production transport wiring.

## Further Notes

The service is currently in memory. Expiration represents domain validity and does not delete invite records.
